Eleanor / team — I pulled together the initial technical artifacts. Quick clarifications and what's attached: 

- Isolation model: Redwood Private uses a split control/data plane. The control plane runs in our managed control VPCs; customer workloads run in tenant VPCs that are connected via a transit gateway with strict route tables. We enforce one-way control-plane connections using application-level mTLS and network ACLs; tenant subnets have no static routes to control-plane management networks.
- Egress: tenant egress is routed to a dedicated NAT + proxy tier in the tenant's VPC or through a managed egress appliance (depending on deployment). All outbound flows are logged at the proxy; logs are exported to the customer's logging bucket or to our audit pipeline (we can provide a sample).
- KMS/HSM: customer keys are stored in their KMS (customer-managed key material) when using Private with KMS integration. In on-prem cases we support HSM-backed keystores; the control plane never stores plaintext keys.
- Evidence we can include: firewall ACL snippet (redacted), transit route table snapshot, proxy access logs (redacted), and an annotated network diagram.

Attachments included here (stubs): network-isolation-diagram-v1.pdf; segmentation-evidence-index.csv

Note: the diagram is intentionally high-level — let us know if Acme's auditors need a stack-level breakout (we can produce a layer-by-layer schematic but need 1 business day).

-Kim
